full_judgment:
4. The case of the plaintiffs, in brief, is that the suit 7.13 acres of land of Ka schedule originally belonged to CS recorded tenant Mohendra Narayan Chakraborty under the Zaminder Gopi Ballav Sen. In the said land there was a temple in .02 acre of land of CS Plot No.1590. One Keramatullah, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs was the nearest neighbor of said Mohendra Narayan Chakraborty who took a loan of Taka 500 from said Keramatullah for the cost of the marriage ceremony of his son. Mohendra Narayan Chakraborty repaid Taka 100 and Taka 50 on 29th Bhadra, 1334 BS, and 18th Bhadra, 1337 BS respectively but died without paying the rest. Mohendra Narayan lost his 1st wife Labonno Prova, and then he married Binhu Basini as his 2nd wife and gave her some valuable properties including the suit land orally as a gift. Mohendra Narayan died leaving behind 03 sons and 01 daughter. After the erosion of the river, he constructed some other tin-shed houses on the bank of the pond named Alordighi for his labor, cattle, and storage on the northern side of the Mosque. On the death of Mohendra Narayan his property devolved upon his widow Bindu Bashini and 03 sons and only daughter Aboya. Previously there was no existing mosque; rather, at that time, there were so many mosques in the nearest Mouja named East Bichandhai. Bindu Bashini while enjoying the suit property peacefully RS Khatian was wrongly recorded in the name of CS recorded tenants. Despite that, .09 acre of land of RS plot No.1852 is rightly recorded in the name of the Mosque which has been constructed by said Keramatullah. No record has been prepared in respect of 0.02 acres of land in the name of the temple. The 03 sons of said Mohendra Narayan partitioned their non-suited land amicably vide a registered deed of partition dated 09-5-1939. Kamakhya Nath Chokraborty, son of Mohendra Narayan Chokraborty sold his entire 8.37 acres of non-suited land to said Keramatullah by a registered sale deed dated 24-1-1952. Girish Chandra Chokraborty, another son of Mohendra Narayan Chokraborty also sold his entire 8.56 acres of non-suited land to said Keramatullah by registered sale deed No. 271 dated 14-1-1952 who took the same in the name of his god daughter Prova Debi. The part of non-suited land that fell in the share of Bindu Bashini, by virtue of the said amicable partition, was looked after by her son Dinesh Chandra. After the death of Labonno Prova, Dinesh Chandra married 2nd time and for that purpose, his mother Bindhu Bashini took a loan of Taka 700 from Keramatullah and thereafter, took another sum of Taka 1350 as a loan to defray the cost of the marriage of her daughter named Aboya but could not repay the same. As a result, the relationship between the families became worsen giving rise to litigations. Keramatullah ultimately took over the possession of the said land of Bindhu Bashini in 1958 adversely. In CR Case No. 287 of 1959, the said Bindu Bashini and Dinesh Chandra also admitted the same. Keramatullah purchased 17 sheets of corrugated tin and donated the same to the local Hindu community to construct a temple there within the suit property. Local Hindus also excavated a pond therein within the suit property named Alor Dighi to avoid a flood of Tista River. Keramatullah took over Alor Dighi on 1-5-1365. Local Hindus took the matter to the then District Magistrate, on 28th Ashwin, 1365 BS, and the Local Sub-Divisional Officer asked the Officer-in-charge of the Hatibanda Thana to submit a report to that effect but the same was kept with the record due to the non-availability of the witnesses. Subsequently, the local Hindu and Muslim community jointly tried to dispossess Keramatullah but failed. Thus, Keramotullah had been enjoying the same peacefully but in the Diara Surv.,y & Settlement Operation the property wrongly recorded in the name of Purba Bichandhai Mosque in respect of 0.09 acres out of 7.25 acres of land. Keramotullah died in 1969 leaving behind the plaintiffs as his legal heirs and now they possess the suit land since 1948. They were unaware of the S.A. record. But the moment the plaintiffs came to know about the same, they filed the instant suit. 

 5. Defendant Nos. 2-10 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying the averments made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form, and bad for defect of parties. Keramotullah was a very influential person. The CS recorded tenant Mohendra Narayan Chokraborty before leaving Pakistan for India, settled the suit property measuring 7.15 acres of land to Pachim Bichondai Mosque. The then Motwalli leased out some lands and possessed the rest. The bank of Alor Dighi was very wide and kept uncultivated for decades together and, both Hindus and Muslims of that vicinity had been using the same by performing their religious rites and rituals. But the SA Khatian was wrongly prepared in the name of the CS recorded tenants. During Diara operation, the settlement Officer after finding the Paschim Bichandai Mosjid there in the suit property recorded the same in the name of the Mosque. The Motwalli was supervising the suit land, as such, the suit be dismissed with cost.
